items.statement: Indian primary market saw 53 issues mobilizing INR 6,895 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, the Indian primary market saw 53 issues collectively mobilize approximately INR 6,895 crores.

items.statement: Mainboard IPO activity decelerated significantly vs FY26 record of 108 issues raising INR 1.76 lakh crores
items.quote: The mainb oard activity represents a significant and disciplined deceleration compared to the record -breaking volume of the preceding financial year, FY26, where 108 mainboard companies raised over INR 1.76 lakh crores

items.statement: SME pipeline remained active with steady filings and small issue sizes protecting from institutional capital volatility
items.quote: The SME pipeline, meanwhile, remained active w ith steady filings, though individual issue sizes remained small, which continues to protect this segment from institutional capital volatility

items.statement: Domestic equity market participation remained robust supported by growing investor base and financialization of savings
items.quote: At the same time, domestic participation in the equity market has remained robust, supported by a growing inves tor base and increasing financialization of savings

items.statement: Signed 3 new advisory mandates in Q1 FY27 reflecting continued origination strength
items.quote: Turning to the operational highlights for the quarter, we signed 3 new advisory mandates, reflecting the continued strength of our origination engine.

items.statement: Secured listing mandate with West Bengal-based ferroalloy company and filed DRHP for Sky Alloys and Power Limited on NSE and BSE
items.quote: We secured a listing mandate with a West Bengal-based ferroalloy company, and we filed the DRHP for Sky Alloys and Power Limited on both NSE and BSE.

items.statement: Bahutex received Category-II AIF registration during quarter with Gretex as partner in the fund
items.quote: On the alternative investment front, Bahutex received its registration for a Category-II AIF during the quarter, with Gretex as a partner in the fund.

items.statement: Expect minimum 3 to 4 IPO listings in current quarter Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yeah, in terms of listing, if I am not wrong on the question, for the current quarter which is going on, we expect a minimum of 3 to 4 IPO listings should happen.

items.statement: Gretex Share Broking Limited continues to progress towards proposed listing with strong contribution this quarter
items.quote: Our subsidiary, Gretex Share Broking Limited, continues to progress towards its proposed listing, and its strong contribution this quarter reaffirmed the strategic value of scaling our broking and market-making operations.

items.statement: Actively engaged in preparatory work for broking subsidiary listing to strengthen platform and support next phase of growth
items.quote: We remain actively engaged in the preparatory work for the same, which we believe will further strengthen the platform and support the next phase of growth.

items.statement: Liquidity conditions in secondary markets stable, important for SME ecosystem and market-making and broking services relevance
items.quote: Liquidity conditions in the secondary markets have been stable, which is particularly important for the SME ecosystem and reinforces the relevance of market-making and broking services.

items.statement: Gradual shift towards professionally managed investment solutions with rising interest across mutual funds, PMS and alternative investment platforms
items.quote: We are also seein g a gradual shift towards professionally managed investment solutions, with rising interest across mutual funds, PMS and alternative investment platforms

items.statement: Industry navigating headwinds from evolving geopolitical uncertainties but confident in long-term growth prospects of Indian capital markets
items.quote: While the industry continues to navigate headwinds arising from evolving geopolitical uncertainties, we remain confident in the long-term growth prospects of the Indian capital markets.

items.statement: Prioritizing execution excellence while building scale across merchant banking and broking platforms in measured and sustainable manner
items.quote: Looking ahead, we will continue to prioritize execution excellence while building scale across our merchant banking and broking platforms in a measured and sustainable manner.

items.statement: Independent Directors confirm they are actively working on structural simplification of MFSL to address holding company discount
items.quote: We also recognize the key role being played by ICICI Prudential AMC as a significant shareholder in MFSL. So, trust us that we are very heavily seized of this issue, and we would find a way out.

items.statement: Independent Directors state structural simplification is a top agenda item discussed in every board meeting with management
items.quote: Let me reassure you that this is one of the items discussed in each meeting formally/informally with management to find a way out, and whatever little guidance and help we can do, we always do that.

items.statement: Independent Directors acknowledge ICICI Prudential AMC's suggestion to publicly disclose options under consideration for structural simplification
items.quote: So, I respect your suggestion. Let us discuss internally. But if you, if you are aware of the transactions contemplated with Axis bank, this is already there.

items.statement: Q3 raw material basket cost expected to rise 4-5% QoQ; NSR planned increase of 4-5% in Q3
items.quote: And our guidance going ahead for Q3 would be a further increase of about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Capex for balance of FY27 estimated at ~Rs 500 crore after Rs 800 crore spent in H1
items.quote: This is going to be roughly around INR500 crores for the balance period.

items.statement: Volume growth from new capex expected at 1:1 to 1:1.1 asset turnover; Rs 1,130 crore expansion underway, Rs 5,000 crore planned in phases
items.quote: The volume growth on account of the capex would be roughly around 1:1 the asset turn, which we are expecting rather 1:1.1 you can consider because we are now taking up expansions immediately for INR1,130 crores, which is going on and then thereafter in phases for around INR5,000 crores capex.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 7.1% in Q2 from 6.8% in Q1; some margin improvement expected in Q3 despite raw material cost pressure
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q2FY27 was recorded at Rs.343 crore as compared to Rs.268 crore in Q1FY27, up by 28% sequentially. 3. EBITDA margins (Consolidated) were recorded at 7.1% v/s 6.8% in

items.statement: Raw material basket up 9% QoQ in Q2 (cumulative 30% in 6 months); NSR increased 7% QoQ in Q2 (cumulative 11-12% in 6 months)
items.quote: We have seen the raw material whole basket increased by 9% on a Q-o-Q basis, which is on a Q1 to Q2 basis. We have seen, obviously, because of the inflationary pressure and supply chain constraint because of the West Asia. Cumulatively, we have seen a staggering 30% increase in the last 6 months.

items.statement: Crude-linked raw materials (65-70% of basket) including carbon black, synthetic rubber, butyl, steel cord all increased YoY and QoQ; no availability issues
items.quote: As you know that crude oil-based raw material is almost in the tune of about 65% to 70%. And there, definitely carbon black, synthetic rubber, butyl, steel cord, they have all increased on a Y-o-Y basis and even on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy with steady momentum expected in Q3 and Q4; replacement market growth continuing
items.quote: We see the demand being steady in Q3. And Q4, as we know, that will be the year-end closing for most of the OEMs also, there will be good demand coming in.

items.statement: Farm sector seeing some traction from rural income improvement but rain deficit may pressure farm season
items.quote: Yes, we are seeing some traction coming in from the farm sector. And there, definitely some increase in terms of rural income has also seen some positive offshoots. Simultaneously, there has been some deficit in terms of rain in some agriculture sector. So that might put a little bit of pressure on farm season, which could go on.

items.statement: Highest-ever consolidated revenue of Rs 4,850 crore in Q2, up 20% YoY; domestic sales up 32% YoY with OE up 65%
items.quote: Coming to JK Tyre in Q2FY27, we have achieved our highest-ever turnover of Rs.4,850 crore, up by 20% on a Y-o-Y basis. This performance was broad-based across markets & product segments. India's business has picked up significant growth momentum post GST 2.0 with an increase in OE sales by 65%, resulting in 32% growth in overall domestic sales on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Domestic volumes up 22% YoY (OE 25%, replacement 20%); TBR OE volumes up 76%, PLR OE up 35%; 2/3W replacement volumes more than doubled
items.quote: 1. Domestic markets recorded a healthy volumes growth of 22%, driven by a robust 25% in OE Market and a similar 20% in replacement markets. 2. TBR volumes in OE market grew by 76% and in replacement market by 9%, YoY 3. PLR volumes witnessed an overall growth of 14%, led by OE market growth of 35% YoY

items.statement: Exports from India up 14% QoQ; Mexico exports to US showing triple-digit volume growth QoQ
items.quote: Despite geopolitical uncertainties, export from India were up by 14% on a sequential basis over Q1FY27.

items.statement: Capacity utilization in India above 90% across key segments (TBR, PLR, 2/3W)
items.quote: Capacity utilization levels in India remained high at above 90% across key segments including TBR, PLR, 2/3W etc.

items.statement: Rs 1,400 crore projects recently completed; Rs 1,130 crore expansion underway; Rs 5,000 crore planned in phases
items.quote: And the 2 nd point is because we have undertaken certain expansion projects for TBR and PCR in addition to what we have completed recently for INR1,400 crores projects.

items.statement: Net debt increased Rs 751 crore QoQ to Rs 5,696 crore due to 30% raw material price increase raising inventory values and higher volumes; working capital expected to improve with operating efficiencies
items.quote: Consolidated Net debt as on 30.09.26 stood at Rs.5,696 Cr, up by Rs.751 crore on QoQ basis. The overall debt of the company has moved primarily on account of increased capex led long-term borrowings and additional working capital requirement for higher raw material prices and higher volumes.

items.statement: Inventory up due to 30% raw material price increase in 6 months, volume growth, and strategic raw material inventory build
items.quote: Inventory has gone up for 2 reasons, one, there has been an increase in the raw material prices to the extent of about 30% in the last 6 months since the West Asia crisis started and also because of volume increase, and Second, we have also kept some strategic inventory in raw material.

items.statement: Net debt to equity at 0.94x as of 30.09.2026; balance sheet healthy with key ratios at acceptable levels
items.quote: The Balance Sheet of the company continues to remain healthy with key financial ratios remaining in acceptable levels viz. Net debt to equity at 0.94x on 30.09.2026.

items.statement: Premium SKUs (16 inch & above) constitute nearly 30% of passenger line volumes in H1, growing at ~20% CAGR over 2-3 years
items.quote: At JK Tyre, nearly 30% of passenger line volumes sold in H1 are towards premium SKUs i.e. 16 inch & above tyres. This segment has maintained a high CAGR of nearly 20% over the past 2-3 years, underscoring the shift in consumer preferences.

items.statement: EV volumes surged 24% QoQ; leadership in electric truck & bus segment; MG Hector Tomahawk launched on Ranger HPe EV tyre
items.quote: At JK tyre, electrification continues to drive a meaningful surge in overall volumes sold across segments and in line with this, we are proud to share that our EV volumes have surged by 24% over the previous quarter. I would like to specially mention our leadership position in the electric truck & bus segment.

items.statement: Added 250+ Pitstops, 80+ new dealers (50% rural), several mobility fleet accounts; expanded OTR range with premium application-specific products
items.quote: In order to strengthen our customer reach, we have further added numerous brand shops, 250+ Pitstops and several mobility fleet accounts during the quarter. Apart from the above, 80+ new dealers have been onboarded in Q2 out of which nearly 50% are rural dealers & distributors.

items.statement: Standalone market mix: replacement 60%, OEM 30%, exports 10%; category mix: TBR 56%, PLR 28%, 2/3W 6%, non-truck bias 10%
items.quote: mix for the replacement market mix is 60%, the OEM is 30% and export is 10% of the total revenue on standalone basis. JK Tyre & Disha Shah: And category mix? Sanjeev Aggarwal: And category-wise, truck and bus is around 56%, PLR is 28%, 6% is 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler and 10% is non-truck bias

items.statement: Evaluating India-UK FTA benefits; developed Europe-specific SKUs; already supplying parts of Europe through exports
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating India - U.K. trade tariff agreement right now. And as I had mentioned earlier in the call that we are developing and developed many Europe specific SKU's . So that we will be definitely taking advantage of the welcoming FTA. And we are already supplying parts of Europe through our exports.

items.statement: JK Tornel revenue Rs 479 crore, EBITDA Rs 23 crore in Q2; expecting normal sales comparable to last year by Q4; Mexico-to-US exports triple-digit volume growth QoQ
items.quote: I am pleased to share that our financial performance witnessed a significant improvement during the quarter, with total revenue reaching Rs.479 crore and EBITDA of Rs.23 crore, reflecting the positive impact of the measures undertaken by the management.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creating inflationary pressure on crude-linked raw materials; raw material cost guidance assumes prices remain in current range through Q4
items.quote: However, recent developments around the resurgence of West Asia conflict remains a critical factor, given their implications for India's inflation, external balance and corporate profitability.

items.statement: Targeting INR 1 lakh crore annual sales; FY27 production target of ~11 million tons net steel (4.79 Mt H1, ~6 Mt H2)
items.quote: Our aim is to reach to about 11-million-ton production in this financial year as targeted earlier. We have reached to a level of about 4.79 million tons in H1. And the next, that is H2, we are aiming for 6 million tons.

items.statement: Annual growth capex guidance of INR 7,500-10,000 crores; H1 FY27 capex INR 3,187 crores
items.quote: Our stated framework envisages annual growth capex of approximately INR 7,500 crores to INR 10,000 crores, primarily funded through internal accruals, while seeking to maintain net debt to EBITDA below 1.5x through the cycle.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA target below 1.5x through the cycle; currently at 1.51x
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved from 1.71x to 1.51x. Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 7,237 crores, providing substantial liquidity as we execute our growth program.

items.statement: Remaining capex of INR 8,000-9,000 crores out of INR 47,000 crore plan for DRI2 and other projects
items.quote: On the INR 47,000 crores of the capex number, we have around INR 8,000 crores to INR 9,000 crores available for the remaining plant like, DRI2 and other things to be completed and at the same time, some pending payments, which will be linked to the performance.

items.statement: Angul blast furnace ramping to 10,500 tpd in 7 days, 11,000 tpd in November, 12,000 tpd in December
items.quote: Hopefully, we will ramp it up in this particular month, say, today is 23rd, so I think in 7 days' time, we should reach to about 10,500 tons per day. And in November, we are aiming for 11,000 tons and then December 12,000 tons per day.

items.statement: 192 km slurry pipeline commissioned; commercial supplies starting in 2-3 days at 20,000 tpd
items.quote: 192-kilometer-long slurry pipeline is already commissioned. The commercial supplies from Barbil to Angul will be starting, I think, in next 2-3 days' time. All trials are done. The first batch of iron slurry has been dispatched and well received.

items.statement: New pellet plant expected commercial production by June 2027; installation complete by March, trials by April
items.quote: Hopefully, by June next year, this will be fully commissioned. So, by March, we will be doing the complete installation. And maybe end of March or early April, we'll start our trials. And June, it should be in commercial production.

items.statement: DRI plant (2 Mt) and 3 gasifiers (105,000 Nm3/hr) targeting commissioning by June 2027
items.quote: The DRI plant will be commissioned again in June 2027. This has already come up. So, there are certain equipment which are imported. So, because of the shipping issues and all these things. So, this may delay. But June, yes, we'll be in production.

items.statement: Exports at ~100,000 tons/month (HRC, plates, rails, structures); targeting EU market access via FTA
items.quote: The exports are also picking up. We are doing about 100,000 tons of export every month, mainly hot-rolled coils, plates and some quantity in rails and the structures.

items.statement: Targeting 65% flat products (incl. plates) / 35% long products mix; Q2 value-added mix 57% (up to 65% on comparable basis)
items.quote: We are now aiming to increase our overall product mix towards flat products. Though today also, we are at a level of about 60% -40%. Now we'll be reaching somewhere about 65%-35%, 65% flat products, including plates and 35% will be long products.

items.statement: Coking coal cost impact $20-25/t in Q3; West Asia conflict diesel impact $4-5/t continuing; propane-to-syngas switch saved INR 70/kg
items.quote: the coking coal inflation, right, just to be sure. Sandeep Modi: No, coking coal, I said $20 to $25. And for the West Asia conflict, which I think you are reflecting more on the diesel and other part, we did not give INR 1,200, INR 1,300. We said around $4 to $5, and that continued to be around $4 to $5 per

items.statement: Water consumption reduced to 31 MLD from 59 MLD sanctioned; slurry pipeline returns water for recycling, further reducing need by 15% next year
items.quote: We do not need 59 MLD now. We are using only 31 MLD, which is sufficient. And in next year, we'll be using at least 15% less. Why? Because we are pumping water from Barbil. So, this water will be surplus.

items.statement: Q2 adjusted EBITDA INR 2,504 cr (+34% YoY), EBITDA/t INR 10,529 (+5% YoY); sequential moderation due to higher raw material and operating costs
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,504 crores, up 34% Y-o-Y, while adjusted EBITDA per ton increased 5% Y-o-Y to INR 10,529 per ton. The sequential moderation in EBITDA was primarily due to higher raw material and operating costs, notwithstanding the positive impact of higher volume and improved sales mix.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand growing ~10% YoY; JSPL production up 20%; Q3/Q4 optimistic on construction pickup and festival season
items.quote: The steel scenario is very good. I think it is now around 10% Y-o-Y basis, there's a growth. Though our production has gone up by 20%. The industry overall growth is about 10%. So, we are aiming that we'll continue making such performance in other 2 quarters also, that is Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: TMT production cut from 220k to 120k tpm; shifted volume to value-added flats (plates, high-carbon HRC); plates >220k tpm, undisputed leader
items.quote: Historically, we were doing about 20% of our total production. We were selling through TMT route. So, TMT was not doing very good in last quarter. So, we increased the volume of hot-rolled coil and reduced the volume of TMT. So, TMT now we are selling only to the major projects. And we are not selling for the retail market in that proportion that we used to do it. So, I would say that now we are m

items.statement: EU steel deficit 28 Mt; India first chance to supply; CBAM issue but Govt negotiating FTA for favoured supplier status
items.quote: There's a steel deficit of about 28 million tons in Europe. And I think India stands the first chance to supply the right and good quality of steel to Europe. CBAM is an issue today. But overnight, the CBAM cannot be diluted. I think EU Parliament and Government of India will find some solution how to meet out the demand of the local people there in Europe.

items.statement: Government offering 50% royalty exemption for coal gasification projects; DRI/CGP expansion benefiting from scheme
items.quote: Government is open to provide coal and with the exemption of 50% of royalty. So, this is one. And secondly, from our own mines also, we'll be in a position to feed the coal gasification. No problem.

items.statement: Net debt reduced INR 1,141 cr QoQ to INR 14,786 cr; net debt/EBITDA 1.51x; cash INR 7,237 cr
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt declined by INR 1,141 crores from INR 15,927 crores at the end of June to INR 14,786 crores as at September end. Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved from 1.71x to 1.51x. Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 7,237 crores, providing substantial liquidity as we execute our growth program.

items.statement: Manpower stable; middle/upper-middle management elevated; no exodus in recent months
items.quote: The manpower is stable. There is no churning. The people from the middle management and upper middle management, those who are at a level about AGM, DGM, general managers, Assistant Vice President, they are being elevated to take the higher responsibilities. And there is very positive atmosphere in the organization. And fortunately, in last couple of months, there is no exodus from the organizatio

items.statement: Geopolitical risk: prolonged West Asia conflict could add another $20/t coking coal cost; water availability risk mitigated by slurry pipeline recycling
items.quote: But just for the factor of safety, we are considering that maybe if this prolongs and there's no decision taken by superpowers, the 2 superpowers, I will say, to end this war and to relax the sanctions on Iran and/or on Russia, then there may be an impact of another $20 in times to come.

items.statement: Q2 sales volume 2.38 Mt (record); NSR INR 16,704 cr (+43% YoY); HRC spot ~INR 60,000, TMT spot ~INR 60,000
items.quote: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly gross revenue of INR 19,448 crores, up 44% Y-o-Y, while net revenue increased 43% Y-o-Y to record INR 16,704 crores. This was driven by the record Q2 sales volume, as Mr. Sharma said, of 2.38 million tons and higher average selling prices, supported by a higher share of flats and a lower proportion of TMT within the long products.

items.statement: Coal gasification plant enabled switch from propane/natural gas to syngas during supply shortage; no productivity/profitability impact
items.quote: We have seen in last 3 months' time, very topsy-turvy situation, where we found that there was a shortage of natural gas in the country and there was a shortage of propane. And this was difficult time basically because of this Hormuz issue or the Iran and U.S. war. So fortunately, we are having the coal gasification plant. And we switched over to coal gas, that is, syngas for many of the reheating

items.statement: Transmission capex expected at INR14,000 crore for FY27 with INR8,000-9,000 crore in H2
items.quote: We expect to do total capex of transmission in the range of about INR14,000 crore. So we will be doing about INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores of capex in second half.

items.statement: Smart Metering installation target revised to 8-9 million meters for FY27
items.quote: So we plan for about 80 to 90 lakh meters this year. And the balance about 40 lakh, 45 lakh, we hope that we will be able to complete in the next half year.

items.statement: Energy Solutions platform targets 7,000-8,000 MW consumer-side tie-ups over 3-4 years
items.quote: So we will continue to scale up this volume, and we will reach to about total aggregate capacity on both sides about 7,000 megawatts to 8,000 megawatts of tie up over 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: H1 FY27 capex deployment at all-time high of INR7,850 crore across all businesses
items.quote: We have deployed about INR7,850 crores of capex in among all our businesses.

items.statement: Transmission capex pipeline projects INR6,000 crore in H2 FY27 and INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28
items.quote: We actually expect to incur to INR6,000 crores additional capex in the second half of this year and another INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores in the FY '28.

items.statement: Transmission order book stands at INR87,000 crore including recently won Vizag and Satara projects
items.quote: And with these two projects, our order book remains at about INR87,000 crores.

items.statement: Smart Metering order book 60% delivered (14.8 million meters), balance to complete in 12-14 months
items.quote: Smart Metering, we have now delivered about 14.8 million meters so far. And around 60 percentage of our order book, that we have delivered and balance portion, we wish to complete in another 12 to 14-month time.

items.statement: Energy Solutions platform delivered revenue >INR2,000 crore and EBITDA >INR800 crore in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During this quarter, the platform delivered revenue of over INR2,000 crores and EBITDA of over INR800 crores.

items.statement: Mumbai distribution consumption increased >10% in H1 FY27 while losses reduced to 4.29%
items.quote: Our Distribution losses in Mumbai has reduced further to 4.29 percentage in the first half. And this despite the fact that consumption has also increased by more than 10 percentage.

items.statement: Energy Solutions consumer stack includes 2,500 MW MSEDCL, 750 MW AEML, 400 MW C&I clients, and advanced data center discussions
items.quote: So one, obviously, you have 2,500 megawatts of the MSEDCL PPA, 750 megawatt of AEML, so that's 3,250 megawatts. We are targeting multiple data center customers. We are in advanced discussions with them. Then further, we also have close to 400 megawatts of C&I clients

items.statement: MSEDCL PPA phased: 1,000 MW from Feb-end, 1,000 MW from Apr-end, 500 MW from Jul-end next year
items.quote: 2.5 gigawatts MSEDCL signed, the capacity starts being deployed from end of February this year, 1,000 megawatts, then 1,000 megawatts from end of April and then another 500 megawatts end of July in the next year.

items.statement: Transmission ROW issues in Gujarat (Halvad) being discussed at State and Central government levels, resolution expected soon
items.quote: Halvad is stacked up because of the ROW problem. And we expect resolution very soon. In fact, it is being discussed at Government of Gujarat as well as our Government of India level very frequently.

items.statement: 75-80% of debt portfolio on fixed coupon basis; ECB ~10% of INR51,000 crore total debt
items.quote: All our USD bonds modes and ECBS, the interest rates are fixed. So 75% to 80% of our debt portfolio is on fixed coupon basis.

items.statement: Significant portion of debt fixed rate or hedged; no material FX or interest rate volatility expected in P&L
items.quote: A significant portion of our debt is also the fixed rate or hedged appropriately. So we don't expect much of the volatility due to foreign exchange or interest rate realization in our P&L or balance sheet.

items.statement: Asset base INR83,000 crore with locked-in capex >INR100,000 crore to deliver in 4-5 years (1.3-1.4x growth)
items.quote: Currently, we have asset base of about INR83,000 crores. And we have already locked in capex of more than INR100,000 crores and that we will be delivering in another 4 to 5 years. So asset will grow almost 1.3x, 1.4x from what we have today in next 5 years.

items.statement: S&P Global Electric Utility ESG rank #1 globally with 90/100 score vs industry average 40
items.quote: We are happy to say that now in S&P Global Electric Utility category, we are number one globally, getting 90 out of 100 rank, where industry average is about 40.

items.statement: Transmission commissioning delays on Khavda-Halvad (ROW), Navinal may spill to H1 FY28; WRSR, Khavda Phase 4, Mahan Phase 1 targeted for FY27
items.quote: We'll be commissioning WRSR, Khavda phase 4, Halvad and Navinal, probably we might be able to commission. And in Mahan as well, phase 1 will get commissioned, the phase 2 will be in next year first quarter.

items.statement: Trading average realization ~INR5.75/unit; power management/trading margin ~INR0.02-0.03/unit
items.quote: See, the average realization as far as trading is concerned is about INR5.75. And what we sell on exchange on behalf of others, we get about INR0.02 to INR0.03 per unit.

items.statement: Energy Solutions has 4 GW renewables and 3.5 GW base capacity tied up on supply side
items.quote: We already have a tie-up of 4 gigawatt of renewables and 3.5 gigawatt of base capacity.

items.statement: Potential Smart Metering acquisition opportunities being explored beyond bidding
items.quote: And there could also be an opportunity of acquisition in the market on top of what we get here through bidding.

items.statement: MAT credit assets of ~INR1,500 crore recognized in MEGPTCL and ATIL under new tax regime with corresponding recoverable liability (no P&L impact)
items.quote: There are two companies, MEGPTCL and ATIL, where we have decided to go to the new tax regime and recognize the past paid MAT assets in the books of account which are close to around INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: NIM expected to recover to ~5.8% by Q4 FY27 as excess liquidity is deployed and repo rate hikes benefit
items.quote: Just in terms of how do we see NIMs going forward, we see this recovering to approximately 5.8% by Q4 as some of these excess liquidity would have been definitely put to use by them and also the expected repo rate increase, which we also are factoring for the course of the year.

items.statement: Incremental cost-to-income ratio guided at 55% for FY27, implying operating jaws of ~500 bps
items.quote: So we feel overall this year, i.e., in '27, we can operate the bank at 55% cost -income ratio.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 1.5-1.6% for FY27
items.quote: So we are very comfortable with our 1.5% to 1.6% credit cost guidance?

items.statement: NIM moderated to 5.58% in Q2 FY27 from 5.90% in Q1 due to FCNR lending (16 bps), excess liquidity (7 bps), asset mix (5 bps) and day count (4 bps)
items.quote: The net interest margin for the quarter was 5.58% as compared to 5.90% in the previous quar ter, excluding the income tax refund, which we have reported

items.statement: FCNR impact on ROA estimated at only 2 bps as lower opex and credit cost on expanded base offset NIM drag
items.quote: The one point which I want to sort of also put across is that the margin impact on FCNR should not be viewed in isolation as because FCNR comes in the denominator, it correspondingly also reduces operating expenses and credit costs related to assets. And hence, we have estimated that the overall impact on the ROA could be very minimal as low as 2 basis points.

items.statement: FCNR deposits provide ~1% cost of funds benefit vs domestic deposits due to lower rate, no PSL/CRR/SLR costs
items.quote: Pursuant to the FCNR scheme, we also have estimated an additional benefit of 1%, including statutory benefits, which could accrue to us if we compare this with a normal deposit, which we would have raised otherwise, if these FCNR flows were not there.

items.statement: Mobilized INR 34,390 cr (USD 3.6 bn) FCNR(B) deposits, constituting 10% of total deposits; extended USD 2.6 bn (INR 25,000 cr) leverage to NRI customers, 7% of loan book
items.quote: During the quarter, the bank mobilized INR34,390 crores, which is about USD3.6 billion of FCNR (B) deposit under this scheme. This constituted about 10% of the overall deposit that we have at September 30, 2026. Against this, we also extended leverage of USD2.6 billion, which is in about INR25,000 crores to NRI customers.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 30.1% YoY and 13.6% QoQ to INR 3.47 lakh cr including FCNR; ex-FCNR grew 22.2% YoY and 5.7% QoQ to INR 3.29 lakh cr
items.quote: Moving on to loans. That registered a strong growth of 30.1% on a Y-o-Y basis and 13.6% on a Q-on-Q basis, including FCNR, and that book has now reached about INR3.47 lakh crores. If we exclude the FCNR(B) backed loans, the loan assets on a gross of IBPC basis grew by 22.2% on a Y -o-Y basis and 5.7% on a Q -on-Q basis and was about INR3.29 lakh crores.

items.statement: Customer deposits grew 26.9% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR 3.4 lakh cr; ex-FCNR customer deposits grew 14.1% YoY
items.quote: If I just talk of customer deposits that has crossed INR3.4 lakh crores. It grew by 26.9% on a Y-o-Y basis and 14% on a Q-on-Q basis. This also included FCNR. And if we exclude FCNR deposits, customer deposits grew by 14.1% on a Y -o-Y

items.statement: CASA deposits grew 19.8% YoY to INR 1.66 lakh cr; CASA ratio 47.6% (48.4% average) impacted by FCNR in denominator
items.quote: If I talk of CASA deposits, that grew to now INR1.66 lakh crores. The growth on a Y-o-Y basis was 19.8%, while the CASA ratio for the quarter came to 47.6%, this was lower because of the FCNR deposit mobilization in the denominator. The average CASA ratio still, I would say, was healthy at about 48.4%.

items.statement: GNPA improved 19 bps QoQ to 1.32% (9 bps ex-FCNR); NNPA improved 4 bps to 0.40% (0.43% ex-FCNR); retail GNPA improved to 1.24% (1.36% ex-FCNR)
items.quote: On a headline basis, the gross NPA ratio of the bank improved by about 19 basis points from 1.51% reported in Q1 to 1.32% in Q2 and by 9 bps if we exclude FCNR leverage from the denominator. Similarly, on net NPA, we saw an improvement of 4 basis points to 0.40%.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 99.5% for retail; SMA-1&2 retail improved to 0.72% from 0.77%; MFI SMA-1&2 normalized to 0.6% from 0.7%; overall SMA-1&2 down 4 bps to 0.58%
items.quote: The SMA-1 and SMA-2 book for the retail was at 0.72% in Q2 from 0.77%, which we saw in the previous quarter. SMA 1 and 2 for microfinance further normalized to 0.6% from 0.7 % in the previous quarter. At an overall bank level, SMA 1 and 2 reduced by 4 basis points to 0.58%.

items.statement: Contingency provision of INR 515 cr maintained for macro/geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: The bank continues to hold the contingency provision of INR515 crores created last quarter. This is on a prudent basis, considering the evolving macroeconomic and the geopolitical uncertainties.

items.statement: Core PAT crossed INR 1,000 cr for first time at INR 1,036 cr in Q2 FY27; ROA at 0.93% (would be higher ex-FCNR denominator effect)
items.quote: This quarter on the core, without any adjustments, it is INR1,036 crores. So we feel good about that. I always said that we'll be in kissing distance of 1% ROA. It looks like we will get there. In fact, this quarter also, we had ROA of about 0.93%.

items.statement: Operating profit grew 38.5% YoY and 6.6% QoQ; 3rd consecutive quarter of 30%+ YoY operating profit growth
items.quote: If I talk of operating profit of the quarter, that saw a healthy increase of 38.5% on a Y-o-Y basis and 6.6% on a sequential basis. So for 3 quarters in a row now, we are getting an operating profit increase of upwards of 30%.

items.statement: Credit cards in force crossed 5 million; outstanding book INR 9,875 cr; spends grew 15% YoY
items.quote: With respect to credit cards, happy to report that the cards in force crossed 5 million during the quarter. The book on an outstanding basis stood at INR9,875 crores, and the credit card spends grew at a healthy pace of about 15% on a Y -o-Y basis.

items.statement: MFI book at INR 6,825 cr (2% of funded assets); 97% covered under CGFMU scheme
items.quote: The MFI book saw a marginal increase during the quarter. That book now stands at INR6,825 crores and about 2% of the overall funded assets. 97% of the book is now covered under the CGFMU scheme.

items.statement: Blended cost of funds for FY28 estimated to rise only 5-10 bps over FY27 despite rate hikes, due to high CASA (50% of deposits) and savings rate cuts
items.quote: But overall, overall, I think our own blended cost of funds of FY28, don't take it as a guidance, but I'm just giving you a bit of off -the-cuff estimate that next year should be maybe 3 or 4 or 5 basis points more maybe over this overall cost of funds basis over FY '27, I mean, '28 over '27, give or take, we feel should be able to manage about 5 basis points.

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance commissions may reduce fee income; impact expected to be offset by FCNR benefit (~1%), repo hikes (50 bps), and product mix changes
items.quote: We have estimated the impact as is in the current form that if this has to come, this will definitely reduce our fee income. But we feel that, to a large extent, the impact can be offset by the expected repo increase and the FCNR benefit, which I have talked earlier. We will also continue to work on product mix changes and closely monitor the developments in this regard.

items.statement: CAR at 14.66%, CET1 at 13.01% as of Sep 2026; LCR avg 125% (Sep 139% due to FCNR); excess liquidity to normalize to 115-116% in a month
items.quote: The capital adequacy ratio stood at 14.66% at September with CET1 ratio of 13.01%. On the LCR, the ratio was at 125% on an average for the quarter and with September being at higher at 139% because of the FCNR money, whi ch came in towards the back end of August. Normally, as you would have noted, that normally, we have been maintaining LCR around the 115% mark. Hence, we would continue to deploy

items.statement: Raised debut USD 950 mn offshore bonds from IBU branch after obtaining investment-grade ratings from S&P and CareEdge
items.quote: On the back of the ratings, we also did a debut bond issuance. We almost raised close to $1 billion of bonds. The actual number was US$ 950 million, and these were raised from the offshore IBU branch from marquee international investors.

items.statement: El Nino/drought in Maharashtra, Karnataka being monitored; no immediate portfolio impact seen for Q3/Q4 but watching cautiously
items.quote: We are, of course, very watchful of this El Niño and the impact will cost to us that a couple of states have declared drought, etcetera. We have to see how much portfolio we have to manage that. But as I can see right now, it doesn't look like there's an immediate impact in Q3 or Q4, and then we'll take it as it comes.

items.statement: Corporate book: 76% A-rated and above, 20% BBB, 4% BB and below; near-zero delinquency over 7 years; cost-income ~32-33%; yield ~9.2%
items.quote: A and above rated companies, since you said what kind of customers we lend to in the corporate side, A and above rated companies, we makes 76% of our book. And BBB companies is 76%. BBB companies is 20% and BB and below is 4%. That is a composition. It's quite comfortable actually and with zero default practically. And just imagine 7 years, Piran, no delinquency.

items.statement: Wholesale/business banking growing >30% YoY; mortgage growth minimal; credit card spends up 15% YoY; FCNR leverage 7% of loan book
items.quote: The incremental growth on the loan side during the quarter was primarily driven by mortgage, vehicle loans, consumer loans and a slightly faster growth in business banking and wholesale loans, which individually grew by more than 30% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Liability franchise drag reducing: loss on avg retail liabilities down from 3% to 0.7%; expected to reach zero in ~3 years, lifting ROA from 1.3% to 1.5%+
items.quote: If you see the trend line, we are not planning to lose 0.7% forever. It's coming down. It's coming down from 3% to 2% to 1% to 0.7%. It has to come down to 0. So in other words, you stretch this forward for maybe 3 years from now, you'll find that this number of 0.7% becomes zero, so which means the drag from liabilities will become zero and that 1.3% is 1.3%, which you can see even today.

items.statement: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for rest of FY27 despite industry headwinds
items.quote: We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.

items.statement: Confident of comfortably crossing AUM growth guidance given for FY27
items.quote: we are well poised to continue our strong traction in disbursements in coming quarters, which will help us cross our growth guidance for this year very comfortably.

items.statement: Q2FY27 disbursements at Rs 2,078 crores, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY; AUM at Rs 14,640 crores, up 6.7% QoQ and 14% YoY
items.quote: Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over previous quarter and 74% year -on-year. The loan book also saw robust growth with our A UM at Rs. 14,640 crores, a growth of over 6.7% over the previous quarter and 14% year -on-year.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% in Q2FY27 from 97.7% in Q1; X-bucket collections 99.4% from 99.2%; 30+ DPD down to 11.5% from 12.38%
items.quote: Collections continue to trend very well with our unique customer collection efficiency improving to 98.2% in the current quarter from 97.7% in Q1, along with improvement in X -bucket collections to 99.4% from 99.2% in Q1, which has helped contain forward fl ows. As a result, the current bucket proportion of our A UM rose sharply from 83.3% to 84.78% and 30 plus DPD came down from 12.38% to 11.5%.

items.statement: Slippages eased to 0.68% from 0.70% in Q1; Gross Stage-3 stable at 3.48%; credit cost improved to 1.80% from 1.85%
items.quote: Slippages eased marginally to 0.68% from 0.70% in Q1 and Gross Stage-3 assets were broadly stable at 3.48%, despite macroeconomic headwinds being witnessed across the industry. The credit cost improved to 1.80% of average A UM from 1.85% in Q1.

items.statement: NIM stable at 19.87% vs 19.97% in Q1, up 16 bps YoY; cost of funds on book eased to 8.78% from 8.80%
items.quote: Net interest margin remained broadly stable at 19.87% as against 19.97% in Q1, and was 16 bps higher year-on-year, showing that our spreads have held up despite the drop in yields.

items.statement: Incremental yield hike of ~1% (100 bps) effective October 2026 across risk categories; yields to move from 21-23% to 22.5-23.9% range
items.quote: About 1% Nischint, across the various risk characteristics. So the number what was about 21%-23% or so, now we will get to about 22.5% -23.9% thereabouts. So, 1% is the incremental increase across the various types of customers and risk categories.

items.statement: Expect cost of funds on book to rise 12-15 bps by FY27 exit to ~8.90%; incremental borrowing cost in H2 ~8.70-8.75%
items.quote: our sense is we should be exiting FY '27 with maybe another 12-15 basis points of higher cost of funds on the book compared to where we are today. So, we are roughly at about 875 or thereabouts. We should possibly be ending the year with more around an 8.90% kind of a number.

items.statement: Yield increase on incremental loans will take 24-36 months to fully reflect on book; spread compression of 8-10 bps expected in H2FY27
items.quote: For the half year, you are right, Sanket. What the 10-15 basis points were was how we will exit the FY '27. But if you look at the half year, yes, about 10-12 bps.

items.statement: Availed incremental debt of Rs 825 crores at all-in cost of 8.43% in Q2FY27; bank borrowing share 69% vs 67% in Q1
items.quote: We availed incremental debt of Rs. 825 crores during the quarter at an all-inclusive cost of 8.43% and our cost of funds on book eased marginally to 8.78% from 8.80% in Q1.

items.statement: Variable rate borrowings ~70% of book: 25% MCLR-linked, 30-35% repo/T-Bill linked, 15-18% SOFR/other external benchmarks
items.quote: See, roughly, the variable rate of our book is about 70%, Abhijit . Out of that, 25% will be MCLR-linked, and repo and T -Bill will be about 30%-35%, with SOFR and the other external benchmarks being another 15%-18%.

items.statement: Liquidity at ~Rs 1,300 crores plus unavailed sanctions of ~Rs 1,100 crores as of Sep 30, sufficient for next quarter
items.quote: Our liquidity as on September 30th stood at about close to Rs. 1,300 crores and we also have unavailed sanctions of about Rs. 1,100 crores, which is more than sufficient for us to take care of our requirements over the next quarter.

items.statement: Added 19 branches in Q2FY27; 75 branches added over last year to deepen presence in core geographies
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 19 branches, and over the last one year we have added 75 branches, the clear thought being focusing on deepening our presence in our core geographies and also putting up additional branches in those states, where we have been operating for a while and developed good comfort across various aspects.

items.statement: Disbursement mix: ~26-27% sub-3L, ~51-52% 3-5L, balance >5L; targeting steady state 25-50-25 mix
items.quote: Roughly, we are at about 26%-27% of sub 3 lakhs and another about 51%-52% on the 3-5 lakhs and the rest being in the greater than 5 lakhs. But it will move to a largely 25-50- 25.

items.statement: Top-up loans ~10-15% of disbursements (~Rs 200-300 crores in Q2); incremental disbursal ~50% of outstanding; vintage >=12-18 months, no DPD threshold breach, credit score not deteriorated
items.quote: today I will probably say this number is somewhere around 10%-15% of the overall disbursements. So if you have done about Rs. 2,000 crores in the last quarter, possibly the top-up number will be somewhere around Rs. 200-Rs. 300 crores out of this. And roughly, the incremental disbursal on these top-up loans will be anywhere around 50%.

items.statement: Stage-2 assets down to Rs 1,173 crores from Rs 1,225 crores YoY; PCR ~40% on Stage-3, ~1.73% on overall AUM
items.quote: Even in terms of absolute quantum, the overall Stage-2 assets dropped from about Rs. 1,225 crores as of September 30th, 2025 to Rs. 1,173 crores as of September 30th, 2026. Our PCR continues to be at around 40% on the Stage-3 assets and on overall AUM its about 1.73%.

items.statement: October collections trending in line with July/September; D1C1 expected ~98% in October vs 98% in September
items.quote: For example, September , we did about 98%. We are expecting that number for October to be very close to 98%.

items.statement: October disbursements muted at ~Rs 550 crores; expect pickup in November-December for good QoQ growth
items.quote: See, October will be a little muted, but November and December will get picked up. So, we expect the disbursements to be somewhere around Rs. 550 crores for this month and then pick up in November and December to get to a good growth number over the previous quarter.

items.statement: ROA 8.39% (+28 bps QoQ), ROE 15.25% (+79 bps QoQ); H1FY27 PAT Rs 571 crores (+3% YoY)
items.quote: We have seen improvements to return ratios compared to the previous quarter. ROA was up 28 bps to 8.39%, and ROE up 79 bps to 15.25%. For the first half of this year, we have clocked a PAT of Rs. 571 crores, up 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cost-to-income (incl. credit cost) slightly over 47%; Opex ratio ~7.5% this quarter, ~7.35-7.40% for year; target 6.75-7% over next couple of years via operating leverage
items.quote: Currently, for this quarter, we are roughly about 7.5%. If you look at the year, Sahej, we are about 7.35%-7.40%. Our sense is that this number will trend down at least by 50-75 basis points over the next couple of years. It will take couple of years, but definitely with the operating leverage kicking in, you should see this number somewhere between 6.75%-7%.

items.statement: Written-off loan recovery Rs 13 crores in Q2 (Rs 8 crores in Q1); total NPA + write-off recovery ~Rs 35 crores; expect full-year NPA resolution >Rs 100 crores
items.quote: See, written off accounts, we did about Rs. 13 crores, which is reflecting in the topline. Put together NPAs and written-off accounts, we were at about Rs. 35 odd crores for this quarter.

items.statement: Written-off loan recovery takes 18-24 months due to lack of SARFAESI; expect meaningful recoveries from FY28-29 onwards
items.quote: Manan, typically, it takes about 18-24 months because we don't have the luxury of SARFAESI, given that our loans are less than 20 lakhs. So, we have to go through the legal process, which is a time-consuming process.

items.statement: Active loans ~5.1 lakh (+5% YoY); 35-40% customers have MFI loans, 40-50% have gold loans (30-40% meaningful overlap)
items.quote: Alongside our focus on increasing ticket size, we have also been growing our customer base, with the active loans standing at about 5.1 lakhs, representing a growth of 5% over the previous year.

items.statement: We will have at least 40%-50% of our customers with some kind of gold loans. Meaningful number will be more like a 30%-40% kind of overlap.
items.quote: We will have at least 40%-50% of our customers with some kind of gold loans. Meaningful number will be more like a 30%-40% kind of overlap.

items.statement: Mudra loans up to Rs 20L not seen as competitive overlap due to GST/return requirements; healthy demand persists for Five-Star's borrower profile
items.quote: But how comfortable are the banks in lending to the profile of borrowers that we are lending to? So this has been a questionable fact and we still have a very healthy demand for our loans. So I don't really see either of them being overlapped because there you also need few other points like proper GST registration, your returns and all that, which possibly are things that we don't insist on.

items.statement: Zero impact from IRDAI circular as insurance is pure pass-through; no insurance commission charged to P&L
items.quote: we had zero impact on account of the IRDA ci rcular because we don't charge even a single rupee of insurance commission that comes on to our P&L. Our insurance is a pure pass -through.

items.statement: Karnataka collections improving month-on-month; worst behind us; no drought impact in core states (TN, AP, Telangana = 80%+ AUM)
items.quote: Karnataka is definitely showing improvements in collections on a month-on-month basis. Our very strong belief is that whatever the worst there is in Karnataka, we have already seen that. And we are seeing collection trends definitely improving on a month-on-month basis.

items.statement: Collection and legal infrastructure fully built; opex fully absorbed; no further cost increase on this account; operating leverage to kick in
items.quote: The Opex has fully absorbed the impact of the collection infrastructure and both on the collection infrastructure and on the legal infrastructure, the cost has been fully baked in. So from here onwards, you will not see any increase in cost on account of collection or legal infra.

items.statement: New product line inching closer; more details likely next quarter
items.quote: We have same interest as what we said in last quarter. Maybe in next quarter, I will give you more details about it. And to the shareholders, we are very clear, we are inching towards the new product.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25.5-26.5% for FY27
items.quote: So, as far as the margin guidance is concerned, so we would like to maintain the same guidance , 25.5 to 26.5 %.

items.statement: R&D spend guidance 2.8-3% of revenue for FY27, expected at upper end near 3% including ACTx impact
items.quote: For this fiscal , we expect the R&D spend to be at the upper end of the guidance , which will be close to 3% of the revenue with accounting fo r the impact of ACTx in the R&D.

items.statement: CAPEX guidance 6-7% of revenue for FY27, H1 FY27 at 4.9%
items.quote: The CAPEX as a percentage of revenue is 4. 9% of the total revenue, which is lower than our guidance of 6% to 7% of revenue for FY27.

items.statement: Export growth guidance 20% on constant currency dollar basis for FY27, actual tracking above 30%
items.quote: we gave the guidance of 20% growth rate on a constant currency dollar basis for the export and the actual growth is coming to upward of 30%

items.statement: International business expected to deliver double-digit growth in FY27
items.quote: So, we expect double growth in international business in the Financial Year ‘27.

items.statement: MR headcount increase guidance of 7% for FY27, on track
items.quote: This year, we have said about 7% increase. We are on track with that.

items.statement: Chronic share ambition to add 100-200 bps annually, targeting 50% in 4-5 years
items.quote: our goal and ambition is to add 100 to 200 basis points every year. And our 4 to 5 year ambition is to touch 50%.

items.statement: Consumer healthcare growth expected in single-digit for FY27, recovery expected in FY28
items.quote: Right now, this year we expect that growth will be in single-digit.

items.statement: Domestic revenue ex-consumer grew 15.9% YoY to Rs 3,428 cr in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Revenues of domestic business excluding consumer healthcare increased by 15.9% year-on-year to Rs. 3,428 crores in Q2 & H1 FY27

items.statement: Secondary sales grew 15.7% YoY, 1.1x IPM outperformance (ex-tirzepatide) in Q2 FY27
items.quote: According to IQVIA, our secondary sales grew by 15. 7%, representing a 1.1 x outperformance versus the IPM growth of 14.2 % excluding tirzepatide.

items.statement: Volume growth accelerated to 6.2% in Q2 FY27 from 4.7% in Q1 FY27 and 0.5% in FY25
items.quote: improving volume growth trend from 0.5% growth in FY25 to 2.3% volume growth in FY26, 4.7% volume growth in 1st Quarter this year to now outperforming IPM with a volume growth of 6. 2% in Quarter 2.

items.statement: Chronic therapies outperformed 1.1x IPM, cardiac 19% and anti-diabetic 16% YoY growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Importantly, we continued to outperform the IPM led by 1.1x outperformance in chronic, with 19% year-on-growth in cardiac and 16% growth in anti -diabetic.

items.statement: Acute recovery with 1.1x IPM outperformance, vitamins 26% and gastro 19% YoY growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Recovery in acute continued with 1.1x outperformance driven by 26% year-on-year growth in vitamin and mineral and 19% growth in gastro

items.statement: Anti-infective recovery progressive: 5.4% YoY in Q2 FY27 vs 3.6% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Anti-infective continues to recover quarter-on-quarter with a growth of 5.4% in Q2FY27 versus 3.6% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: BSV key brands strong: Humog 51%, Lonopin 45%, Anti-D 37%, ASVS 45% YoY growth in Q2 FY27
items.quote: BSV business also delivered strong momentum with robust growth in key brands – Humog (51%), Lonopin (45%), Anti-D (37%) and ASVS (45%).

items.statement: Hospital segment revenue grew 23% YoY in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter we saw a strong 23% year-on-year growth in hospital revenues.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 27.1% in Q2 FY27, up 210 bps YoY; H1 FY27 26.7%, up 230 bps YoY
items.quote: Our reported EBITDA margin for the quarter has incr eased to 27.1% as compared to 25 .0% in Q2 FY26. This increase of 210 basis point

items.statement: Gross margin 72.2% in Q2 FY27, up 90 bps YoY driven by price increases, chronic mix improvement, and base effect
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter has increase d by 90 basis point year -on-year basis to 72.2% from 71.3% in Q2 FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion driven 90 bps from gross margin, 40 bps from lower R&D, 80 bps from operating leverage in Q2 FY27
items.quote: 90 basis point increase is from gross margin expansion , reduced R&D expense by 40 basis point and the balance 80 basis point benefit has come from operating leverage due to sales growth.

items.statement: Capex Rs 214 cr in H1 FY27 vs Rs 163 cr in Q2 FY26, at 4.9% of revenue
items.quote: Our CAPEX spent during the quarter has increa sed to Rs. 214 crores in H1 FY27 as compared to Rs. 163 crores in Q2 F Y26.

items.statement: Added 9 new brands >Rs 50 cr (total 63) and 4 new brands >Rs 100 cr (total 26) in MAT Sep 26 vs FY26
items.quote: We have added 9 new brand families with sales over Rs. 50 crores taking the total to 63 in MAT September 26 versus 54 in Financial Year ’26, and 4 brand families with sales over Rs. 100 crores taking the total to 26 from 22 during the same period.

items.statement: Chronic share ex-BSV expanded 80 bps YoY to 37.4% in Q2 FY27, driven by cardio, anti-diabetic, respiratory outperformance
items.quote: our chronic share excluding BSV expanded by 80 bps year -on-year to 37.4 % led by 1.1x outperformance in cardio and anti -diabetes excluding tirzepatide and a strong 1.9x outp erformance in chronic respiratory during the quarter.

items.statement: Modern trade and e-commerce share in consumer healthcare increased to 18% from 12% YoY, 55% channel growth
items.quote: Our modern trade and e-commerce share increased to 18% from 12% a year ago supported by 55% growth in that channel.

items.statement: Gynecologist coverage expanded from 33,000 to 37,000 in last 18-24 months for BSV portfolio
items.quote: Secondly, we've also increased the gyneac coverage over the last 18 -24 months from 33,000 to now 37,000.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs 2,639 cr as of Sep 30, 2026; net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.6x (TTM); on track to repay acquisition debt by FY28
items.quote: we have reduced our net debt to Rs. 2,639 crores as on 30th September 26 resulting in the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 0.6x in Quarter 2 FY27 on trailing 12-month basis. We remain on track to repay the acquisition related debt by FY28.

items.statement: Acquired 70% stake in Armed Cell Therapeutics for CAR-T platform; committed 48M EUR funding through FY28
items.quote: the current commitment, whatever has been done is to the extent of 48 Million Euros and basis an early discussion, so, this is good up to Fiscal Year 2028.

items.statement: Prepared for UCPMP statutory compliance for 7-8 years; fully geared up for Supreme Court mandated committee recommendations
items.quote: we have been preparing for it, not just in the last 3, 4 years, but since the last 7 to 8 years. And we are all geared up. And I think whatever the committee recommends , whatever guidelines they come up with , we are fully geared up to comply with it.

items.statement: Received favorable Commissioner of Appeals order on Rs 1,609 cr Section 37(1) tax demand; exposure reduced by ~Rs 300 cr; fully provided
items.quote: we have received a favorable order from the Commissioner of Appeals. So, wherein they have quashed the four years in the order, favorable order has been passed. And the overall exposure has been brought down from the old level by Rs. 300 odd crores.

items.statement: MR productivity improved to Rs 7.4 lakh (TTM) in Q2 FY27 from Rs 7 lakh YoY despite hiring
items.quote: If you see our field force productivity last year was around 7 lakhs and quarter two ending , trailing 12 months is about 7.4 lakhs. So , despite hiring more people , given the growth, we've been able to improve our MR productivity.

items.statement: Consumer healthcare transformation underway; leadership changes planned in next few months to fix underperformance
items.quote: the kind of transforming changes we brought a few years back in Mankind, the same kind of changes you will see in next few months in consumer side.

items.statement: Revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crores in Q2 FY27; EBITDA more than doubled; fourth consecutive profitable quarter
items.quote: Revenue grew 44% year-on-year to INR 738 crores, EBITDA more than doubled, and this is our fourth consecutive profitable quarter on a standalone basis.

items.statement: Crossed 1 million customers in Q2 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, BlueStone crossed 1 million customers.

items.statement: Launched handcrafted and antique range at flagship store in Kolkata; now have over 10,500 designs
items.quote: The newest, a handcr afted and antique range , launched this quarter at our flagship store on Park Street in Kolkata

items.statement: Opened 27 stores in Q2 FY27; entered 7 new Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
items.quote: All seven new cities we entered this quarter were Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, and customers there chose the same contemporary BlueStone designs as customers in the metros.

items.statement: Redesigned entry-level range taking more space in stores to bring first BlueStone piece within reach of more people
items.quote: Our redesigned entry - level range is now taking more space in our stores, which br ings a first BlueStone piece within reach of many more people

items.statement: Expect AOV growth of 10-15% even when gold prices are flat, driven by repeat customers buying at higher values; buyer growth to drive growth in Q3
items.quote: So, 10%, 15% kind of ticket growth or AOV growth is something that historically, even when gold remained flat, happens as people mature in your system.
